classification.difficultyReason: Identify each instrument's unit, infer the value of unlabelled intervals from labelled graduations, and read the indicated tick; the hardest scale requires dividing a 200 mL span into four intervals.

content.prompt: The diagrams below show the readings for measurements taken using a range of different measuring tools. In each diagram, the arrow indicates what the measurement was. Read the scale and write down the reading. Include the unit of measurement in each case.

spec.description: Ruler with ten subdivisions per centimetre; arrow at the fourth numbered centimetre tick. Decorative ruler fill omitted.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied scale and identifying arrow are visible.

answer.worked: The arrow points to the tick labelled 4 on the centimetre scale, so the reading is $4\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: Tapered vessel with spatially nonuniform graduations 2.5, 5, 10, 20, 30 and 40; liquid and arrow at the 5 graduation. Source yellow liquid maps to light orange.
spec.mathematics: Read a labelled nonuniform capacity scale.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied labels, liquid surface and arrow only.

answer.worked: The liquid surface and arrow align with the graduation labelled 5, so the reading is $5\text{ mL}$.

spec.description: Bathroom-scale arced dial with labels 60, 70 and 80 kg, one-kilogram ticks, and pointer two ticks after 70. Decorative body colours omitted.
spec.mathematics: Ten equal intervals between 70 and 80; indicated reading 72 kg.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied pointer and identifying arrow retained; no answer annotation.

answer.worked: The ten intervals between 70 and 80 each represent $1\text{ kg}$. The pointer is two intervals after 70: $70+2=72\text{ kg}$.

spec.description: Offset ruler segment labelled 11–15 cm with millimetre ticks; arrow at third subdivision after 13. Decorative fill omitted.
spec.answerVisibility: Scale and supplied identifying arrow only.

answer.worked: Each small interval is $0.1\text{ cm}$. The arrow points three intervals after 13, giving $13+0.3=13.3\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: Kitchen scale with labelled 100, 200 and 300 gram marks, ten-gram minor divisions and pointer two divisions after 200. Pan and contents retained as outline; decorative body fill omitted.
spec.answerVisibility: Original pointer, arrow and graduations only.

answer.worked: The ten intervals from 200 to 300 each represent $10\text{ g}$. The pointer is two intervals after 200: $200+2\times10=220\text{ g}$.

spec.description: Jug with horizontal liquid surface, 200–1000 mL labels and four subdivisions per 200 mL; surface at first tick above 600. Light blue fill represents liquid.
spec.mathematics: Each subdivision is 50 mL; surface 650 mL.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied liquid surface and identifying arrow visible; no added answer label.

answer.worked: Four equal intervals represent $200\text{ mL}$, so each interval is $200\div4=50\text{ mL}$. The liquid is one interval above 600: $600+50=650\text{ mL}$.
